You are an expert power-electronics designer synthesising the interface circuit of a
piezoelectric energy harvester. You work by experiment: you propose a circuit, it is simulated in
LTspice under several operating conditions, and you receive the measurements.

GOAL
A piezo transducer must power a sensor-node load RL from a storage capacitor at node "out".
Under EVERY operating condition below, starting from 0 V (cold start) and simulating 0.8 s:
  vout_min: vavg >= 4.5 V (settled mean output reaches the load's minimum supply)
  vout_max: vmax <= 5.5 V (output never exceeds the load's absolute maximum)
  ripple: vpp <= 0.05 V (peak-to-peak ripple in the final window)
  startup: tup <= 0.4 s (cold start: first time output reaches 4.5 V)
  settled: dv <= 0.02 V (mean output changes little between the last two windows)
Measurement windows: vavg and vpp over 0.7-0.8 s; vmax over the whole run; tup = first time
V(out) reaches 4.5 V (missing if never); dv = |mean(0.7-0.8 s) - mean(0.6-0.7 s)|.

PIEZO MODEL AND OPERATING CONDITIONS
The piezo is a sinusoidal current source Ip*sin(2*pi*f*t) in parallel with its capacitance Cp and a
20 MOhm leakage resistance, between nodes pzp and pzn (Cp = 25 nF at S1).
Its open-circuit voltage amplitude is Ip/(2*pi*f*Cp), about 3.8 V at S1; compare it with the
output window and the diode drops.
  S1: nominal; Ip = 60 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S2: heavy load; Ip = 60 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 1000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S3: strong excitation, light load; Ip = 120 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 10000 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S4: weak excitation; Ip = 40 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 4700 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S5: low frequency; Ip = 50 uA peak, f = 80 Hz, Cp = 25 nF, RL = 3300 kOhm, temperature 27 C
  S6: Cp +20 %, hot; Ip = 60 uA peak, f = 100 Hz, Cp = 30 nF, RL = 2200 kOhm, temperature 60 C

TEST BENCH (fixed, added automatically - do not include these)
- the piezo model between pzp and pzn; the load RL from out to 0;
- for every SYNC controller you use, a 0.5 uA supply current drawn from out (its power cost);
- a 1 GOhm resistor to 0 from pzp, pzn and every internal node (prevents floating nodes).

COMPONENTS YOU MAY USE (at most 16 components)
- R  resistor, value 1..1e+08 Ohm, nodes [a, b]
- C  capacitor, value 1e-10..4.7e-05 F, nodes [a, b]
- L  inductor, value 1e-05..0.01 H; it has series resistance 2 Ohm + 5 Ohm per mH
- D  diode, nodes [anode, cathode]: forward current flows from the first node to the second.
     Model one of DSCH, DSI, DZ33:
     DSCH = low-drop Schottky (~0.25 V at uA), DSI = silicon small-signal (~0.5 V at uA),
     DZ33 = 3.3 V zener (reverse breakdown 3.3 V, conducts ~1 uA at 3.3 V and much more above)
     Orientation matters:
       full bridge: ["pzp", "out"], ["pzn", "out"], ["0", "pzp"], ["0", "pzn"] (return diodes have
       their anode on ground);
       zener clamp on out: ["0", "out"] (cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased and breaks down at
       3.3 V). ["out", "0"] would be forward-biased and hold out near 0.7 V; it is rejected.
- S  switch, nodes [a, b], "ctrl": id of a SYNC; Ron = 2 Ohm, Roff = 1 GOhm (at most 4)
- SYNC ideal synchronous controller (no nodes, at most 2): closes its switches for "ton"
     seconds (1e-07..0.001) at the piezo voltage extrema, which occur at the zero
     crossings of the piezo current. "edges": "both" (every half period), "pos" (positive peak only)
     or "neg" (negative peak only). "phase" shifts the pulses by that fraction of the excitation
     period (-0.25..0.25). It tracks the excitation frequency automatically.
     For L-Cp inversion, ton is about pi*sqrt(L*Cp).
Nodes: "0" is ground; pzp, pzn are the piezo terminals; out is the load/storage node; name any other
nodes yourself (lower-case, e.g. n1, mid). Every node needs at least two connections, and out must
connect to the piezo through your circuit.

REFERENCE DESIGN: FBR (full-bridge rectifier, 4 x DSCH, 2.2 uF on out). Its results:

S2       3.18     3.2    44.2       -      10.1  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S3       7.08    7.13     110   0.209      5.01  ok       FAIL     FAIL     ok       FAIL    
S4       2.21    2.22    33.8       -      1.04  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    
S5        3.4    3.44    83.3       -       3.5  FAIL     ok       FAIL     FAIL     FAIL    
S6       2.81    2.83    28.1       -       3.6  FAIL     ok       ok       FAIL     FAIL    

HOW TO WORK
- Component values are optimised automatically (an evolution strategy, up to 48 full
  evaluations per structure, running while you think), so spend your reasoning on circuit
  CONNECTIVITY (topology): which structure can meet every condition. A structure that was already
  explored is not simulated again, whatever its values.
- Each proposal is first SCREENED: with out fixed at 4.5 V, the net power it delivers is
  measured on S2, S4, S6 for its proposed values and a few automatic value presets.
  If the best preset delivers less than 50 % of the load's need (V^2/RL) on any of them,
  the design is reported back with those powers and is not tuned or simulated further.
- Each round, propose up to 3 designs with DIFFERENT connectivity (different structures, not value variants).
- Classify each design with "move": new_topology or modify_topology, and explain the expected effect
  in "rationale". Set "done": true only when you believe no further structural change can improve on
  the best design so far.
- Reply with ONE JSON object only, in this form:

 "proposals": [

    },

    },

    },

    }

  }

}

reply.reasoning:
*   Goal: $V_{out,min} \ge 4.5\text{V}$, $V_{out,max} \le 5.5\text{V}$, $V_{pp} \le 0.05\text{V}$, $t_{up} \le 0.4\text{s}$, $dv \le 0.02\text{V}$.
    *   Piezo: $I_p = 60\text{uA}$ peak, $f=100\text{Hz}$, $C_p=25\text{nF}$, $R_{leak}=20\text{M}\Omega$.
    *   Load $R_L$ varies from $1\text{M}\Omega$ to $10\text{M}\Omega$.
    *   Previous Best: `p_sshi_full_bridge` (Score 43.56). Passed $V_{min}$ for all, but failed $V_{max}$ and some ripple.
    *   Previous Attempt to fix $V_{max}$: `p_sshi_full_bridge_zener_clamp` (Score 18.88). $V_{max}$ is now OK (around 5V), but ripple is too high ($>100\text{mV}$).

    *   `p_sshi_full_bridge` (FBR + SSHI): $V_{out}$ goes too high (S1: 6.9V, S3: 15.3V).
    *   `p_sshi_full_bridge_zener_clamp`: $V_{out}$ is clamped near 5V, but ripple is too high.
    *   Wait, why is the ripple high in the Zener clamp version? Let's look at the components:
        *   $C_1 = 4.6\text{e-07}$ (0.46 uF).
        *   The Zener clamp `DZ1` (DZ33) is in series with 4 DSI diodes (`DC1-DC4`).
        *   Total drop of Zener clamp: $3.3\text{V} + 4 \times 0.5\text{V} \approx 5.3\text{V}$.
        *   Wait, if the clamp is conducting, it's limiting the peak voltage. But it doesn't reduce the *ripple* (which is $\Delta V = I_{load} \times \frac{\Delta t}{C_{out}}$ or similar).
        *   The ripple in the `p_sshi_full_bridge` was $35.7\text{mV}$ (S1), $56.4\text{mV}$ (S2). These are quite close to the $50\text{mV}$ limit.
        *   The ripple in the `p_sshi_full_bridge_zener_clamp` is $104\text{mV}$ (S1, S2). This is much worse. Why?
        *   Looking at the tuning results: $C_1$ is $4.6\text{e-07}$ in both.
        *   Ah, in `p_sshi_full_bridge`, $V_{out}$ was higher (6-15V). The ripple $\Delta V$ is usually absolute. If $V_{out}$ is lower, the relative ripple might be the same, but the absolute ripple depends on the capacitor and the current pulses.
        *   The main issue with `p_sshi_full_bridge` was $V_{max}$. If we can just limit $V_{max}$ without destroying the efficiency or introducing high-frequency noise/losses, we're good.

    *   A simple Zener clamp on `out` would be: `DZ1` anode to `0`, cathode to `out`. But `DZ33` breaks down at 3.3V. We need to clamp at 5.5V.
    *   To clamp at 5.5V using a 3.3V Zener, we need to add diodes in series: $5.5\text{V} - 3.3\text{V} = 2.2\text{V}$. About 4-5 silicon diodes (0.5V each) or a few Schottky diodes.
    *   Wait, if we just want to limit $V_{max}$ to 5.5V, why not use a simpler clamp?
    *   The current `p_sshi_full_bridge_zener_clamp` has:
        `DZ1` nodes `[n2, out]` (cathode on `out`? No, the prompt says "cathode on out, so it is reverse-biased").
        Let's re-read: `DZ1` `n2 out` (so node `out` is cathode). `DC1` `n2 n3`, `DC2` `n3 n4`, `DC3` `n4 n5`, `DC4` `n5 0`.
        So the path is `out` (cathode) $\to$ `n2` (anode) $\to$ `n2` (anode) $\to$ `n3` (cathode) ... $\to$ `0`.
        Wait, `DZ1` is `n2 out`. If `out` is cathode, then it's reverse-biased. Breakdown occurs when `V(out) - V(n2) = 3.3V`.
        Then `V(n2)` is the anode. `DC1` is `n2 n3` (anode `n2`, cathode `n3`). `DC2` is `n3 n4` (anode `n3`, cathode `n4`).
        Total voltage to conduct: $3.3\text{V} + 0.5\text{V} \times 4 = 5.3\text{V}$.
        This clamp is correct. But why the ripple increase?
        Maybe the tuning of $C_1$ was poor? $C_1 = 4.6\text{e-07}$ is quite small. In `p_sshi_half_bridge` (which failed for other reasons), $C_1$ was $2.17\text{e-05}$ (21 uF).

    *   Ripple $\Delta V \approx \frac{I_{load}}{f_{pulse} \cdot C_{out}}$.
    *   $I_{load}$ (S2) $= \frac{5\text{V}}{1\text{M}\Omega} = 5\text{uA}$.
    *   $f_{pulse} = 2 \times 100\text{Hz} = 200\text{Hz}$.
    *   $\Delta V \approx \frac{5\text{uA}}{200\text{Hz} \cdot 0.46\text{uF}} \approx \frac{5\text{e-6}}{9.2\text{e-5}} \approx 0.054\text{V}$.
    *   So $0.46\text{uF}$ is just on the edge. We need a larger capacitor to reduce ripple.
    *   But wait, if we increase $C_1$, the startup time $t_{up}$ increases.
